_readme: Copy to vault/protectedTargets.json and edit. CAIRN never reads this file from examples/. Declaring nothing is safe: consequence is then recorded as 'not assessed' rather than as low, and no grade is raised.
_whatThisDoes: Raises the risk grade of an action according to what it would AFFECT, not only how it would do it. Without it, 'run a script' is MEDIUM whether the script prints a message or reconfigures a production cluster.
_matching: Every match is a literal string or path comparison. The model is never asked what is critical, because the model is the thing being governed.
_criticality: LOW | MEDIUM | HIGH | CRITICAL. A matched target raises the action's grade to this level. A READ of a protected target is recorded but does not raise the grade, because a read does not affect it.
declaredBy: Infrastructure Security — replace with your own team and date

targets.label: Production trading cluster
targets.note: identifiers are matched case-insensitively against the tool name, the argument values, and the resolved execution payload — which includes the contents of a vault script invoked by name, so naming a script cannot evade this.

targets.label: Production configuration root
targets.note: '..' is resolved before comparison and case and separators are folded, so C:\ProgramData\Prod\..\Windows does not satisfy this prefix. A sibling directory sharing the prefix text (Prod-Notes) does not match.

targets.label: Cluster capacity reconfiguration
targets.note: patterns are regular expressions, matched case-insensitively. A pattern that will not compile is REPORTED in the decision record rather than skipped, because an operator with a broken expression believes they have protection they do not have.

targets.label: Anything under the production deployment pipeline
targets.note: A MEDIUM target does not raise a grade that is already MEDIUM or higher. Use it to record that something was touched without changing the outcome.
